line_format.row: - **<CHAR id>** (LN-ep01-NNN): “line” {emotion: <voice.json emotion_range key>, est_duration_s: <s>, style_hits: [<marker ids>]}
line_format.why_changed: v1 rows ('[LN-ep01-NNN] CHAR-alice: “…”') are not parsed by code/check_dialogue_fit.py. Its _SP_LINE_RE only reads '- **who** (paren): body'. Against v1 the checker found 0 lines and would have passed without checking anything. The new row keeps the LN id in the parenthesis, so the checker reads all 34 lines. code/modules/script_breakdown.py also reads all 34 rows (speaker, text, emotion, est_s, style_hits). Note: breakdown puts the LN id in 'paren', not in 'id', because slug CHAR ids do not match its CHAR-\d+ pattern. The screenplay receipt already reported this host-parser limitation.
line_format.emotion_vocabulary: the keys of each speaker's voice.json emotion_range (calm / timid / agitated / whisper / recitation_strange for Alice; calm for the Sister; panicked for the White Rabbit), so voice-generation can map them directly

changes.speaker: CHAR-alice-sister
changes.why: Designed line (no source). v1 matched none of the Sister's markers (0% hit). Her card's endearment rule ('Alice dear') makes it hers. It is still a mild hush from someone who does not look up from her book.

changes.speaker: CHAR-alice
changes.from: Which certainly was not here before.
changes.to: That certainly was not here before.
changes.why: In Carroll the words sit inside narration ('which certainly was not here before, said Alice'). Spoken on its own, a relative 'Which' does not sound like speech. Only the first word changes; 'certainly' is kept.

changes.speaker: CHAR-alice
changes.from: Well, I'll eat it. If it makes me grow larger, I can reach the key;
changes.to: Well, I'll eat it. And if it makes me grow larger, I can reach the key;
changes.why: Puts back Carroll's 'and if' (ch001-d0032), which matches the 'and if' of 013b and her run-on musing pattern.

changes.speaker: CHAR-alice
changes.from: Four times five is twelve, and four times six is thirteen… London is the capital of Paris—
changes.to: Let me see: four times five is twelve, and four times six is thirteen… London is the capital of Paris—
changes.why: Puts back Carroll's own 'Let me see:' (ch002-d0016). It sets up the self-test she acts out by counting on her fingers, and it hits her hedging marker A3. Estimated at 7.7 s, still under the 10.5 s cap.

open_items_for_H3: S01 (from screenplay): is it acceptable to turn the book thought into a spoken line to the sister? If not, the fallback is to play it silently (Alice peeps at the page with no pictures and flops back).

Dream frame continuity (from screenplay): in ep09 Alice wakes on the bank with her head in her sister's lap, but here she runs to the hedge. S01 plants a moment of dozing so the chase can read as her sleep beginning. Please confirm this reading, or rule that the dream starts on the bank.

S10 (new, dialogue-rewrite): 'And in that case I can go back by railway.' refers to a thought the film cuts (that she has fallen into the sea). A viewer may not follow it. Option A: keep it as is (current). Option B: voice the thought as Carroll paraphrase, 'I must have fallen into the sea! And in that case I can go back by railway.' (about 5.5 s, under the cap). B would be a second spoken thought, next to the S01 precedent, so it needs H3 and screenplay sign-off.
S01 (new, dialogue-rewrite): the Sister's designed reply is now 'Hush, Alice dear.' (it was 'Hush, Alice.'). Please confirm the warmer register.
